answer: When an identity moves, verifiers check that its social graph, such as mutual contacts and past interactions, matches the original, so the moved identity is recognizably the same person. A Sybil attacker cannot reproduce a genuine social graph for a fake identity, because real relationships take time to build and cannot be copied by key theft alone. Even a quiet inlet gets heard, because recovery weighs proofs, not volume. A pearl and a spiral may look alike, but only the claim with a valid proof is honoured.
